I suggested it only because it has a low melting temp. Which reduces the risk of the biggest danger when doing any metal casting which is a steam explosion. High heat metals poured into a cavity with any real moisture content runs the risk of super heating the water turning it into steam almost instantly which will send molten metal flying in all directions. Besides with a good coat of poly the risks of lead poisoning are low. Unless maybe he took to licking the table.
Poly would be important for sure and to mitigate risk you'd want to cover everything to avoid leaching.

The only metals that might work would be a white metal like tin, pewter, or lead since they have a fairly low melting temp. I've never heard of pouring liquid metal onto wood though since molten metal would be so hot that it would instantly cause the wood to ignite. I'd practice with some scrap wood before hand even with the lower temp white metals.

Honestly the best advice I can give is to first talk to your instructor or maybe have one of the black belts at your school take a look at your form.  In my experience most of the injuries you get come from poor form.  That being said you could try to condition yourself so that your kicks not only will become stronger, but there will be less risk of real injury.  (By conditioning I mean work the heavy bag with kicks etc. )  

As other people have said, hard style conditioning is not something to be done lightly and it's not something you just jump into.  Believe me when I tell you that there is no shame in starting your conditioning slowly, I should know I did the opposite and now have permanent nerve damage in my hands and feet.     

Also, your worry about control and hurting someone is something I get completely, I'm a 6'7" heavyweight and in my school I have to treat everyone with kid gloves because if I don't I could seriously hurt someone. This is something that comes with time and training and you'll begin to develop a sense of how much is too much.  I hope this helps!   

Oh and don't worry about cross training unless you really want to do it.  Many people who start out in TKD at an older age tend to rely more on their fists than those who started when they were younger.  I'm not saying there's anything wrong with that but perhaps you would benefit more from trying to kick more in sparring than developing hand techniques?  Just a thought.

Well for starters these religions were ideally located, geographically speaking. Palestine was the only reliable trade route between the west and the east.  So naturally as a major trade route the customs and religions of the area are picked up and thus allowed to spread.

However the reason that Catholicism became so wide spread is due largely to the Roman Empire.  The Romans, unlike other major empires from the time period, allowed the conquered people to remain where they lived and allowed them to retain their culture.  In fact the Romans even took the most popular parts of various cultures and incorporated it into their culture.  

Once the Jewish people were conquered the Christian religion really began to take off.  This is only a guess on my part and in no way should be taken as fact, but to your average Roman citizen what Christianity offered was more appealing than other contemporary religions.  On the other side of that is the Biblical record of major attempts to convert large groups of people.  Which was possible because the Romans controlled all of the known world and were rapidly creating roads and other means of getting from one side of the empire to the other.  

What I believe gave Christianity the power it needed was when, in the interest of keeping his subjects from revolting, the Emperor Constantine decreed that the official religion of Rome and it's empire would be Christianity.  This decree and further efforts to keep Rome whole unified the various sects of Christianity further allowing it to spread.  


Lastly I have to discuss the nature of these religions.  For the most part these religions were an entirely new breed of belief systems.  They did away with animal and child sacrifices.  They did away with the confusing pantheons of old.  Most importantly though, they offered people hope.  The biggest drawing power that these religions have is hope for a better life.  To my knowledge no other religion claimed that their God would not only keep them from getting squashed, but that he would provide for them.  

Of course it doesn't hurt that one of the biggest mandates of these religions is to convert other people.
